title: Historical Neighbourhoods vs Ongoing Housing Shifts

sections.content: You know *imperfecto* versus present perfect for change over time from B1 Unit 5, *sin embargo* from B1 Unit 1 and *mientras que* from B2 Unit 28. In urban feature reporting, this tense contrast structures the story of a city: the *imperfecto* sets the enduring baseline of how a neighbourhood used to work (*antes el casco histórico albergaba pequeños comercios*), while the present perfect marks structural shifts whose effects are still felt today (*en la última década el alquiler vacacional ha transformado el tejido vecinal*). Pairing the two clauses with *pero*, *mientras que* or *sin embargo* turns a simple time contrast into a sharp journalistic argument about gentrification and urban density.

sections.title: Framing urban change in feature reporting
rows: Contrasts a former steady state with a current outcome (*Antes el casco histórico albergaba tiendas locales, pero el alquiler vacacional ha desplazado el tejido vecinal.*).
Places a past habit side by side with a present shift (*Durante décadas el barrio mantenía una densidad urbana estable, mientras que hoy la gentrificación ha encarecido la vivienda.*).
Formal journalistic pivot (*Las familias encontraban vivienda asequible cerca del centro; sin embargo, el urbanismo turístico ha reducido esa oferta.*).

items.spanish: Antes el casco histórico albergaba pequeños talleres, pero en la última década el alquiler vacacional ha transformado el tejido vecinal.
items.english: Before, the historic centre housed small workshops, but in the last decade holiday rentals have transformed the neighbourhood fabric.

items.spanish: Durante años las familias encontraban vivienda asequible en el centro, mientras que ahora la gentrificación ha reducido las opciones.
items.english: For years families found affordable housing in the centre, whereas now gentrification has reduced the options.

items.spanish: El barrio mantenía una densidad urbana equilibrada; sin embargo, el nuevo modelo de urbanismo ha cambiado el uso de las calles.
items.english: The neighbourhood maintained a balanced urban density; however, the new model of urban planning has changed how the streets are used.

items.spanish: Antes los vecinos se conocían en la plaza, pero el aumento de los alquileres ha debilitado la vida comunitaria.
items.english: Before, neighbours knew one another in the square, but rising rents have weakened community life.

sections.content: English speakers often put both halves in the simple past (*albergó … transformó*), which turns a living urban trend into a closed anecdote. Keep the *imperfecto* for the long-standing baseline (*antes*, *durante años*) and the present perfect (*en la última década*, *últimamente*) for changes that still shape the city today.
